row.content: progress: during manual smoke preparation for pi memory commit/changelog tools, `.pi/memory.json` in `/home/j0k3r/.pi/agent` was checked and already had `enabled: true` and `git.enabled: true`. json validation passed with `python -m json.tool .pi/memory.json`. `memory_context` resolved project scope to `j0k3r-pi`. a read-only `memory_commit_changelog_search` smoke returned successfully with 0 existing commit/changelog/release records. no git commits, tags, pushes, or config edits were performed.

row.title: git memory duplicate commit records from unnormalized repo urls
row.summary: git memory tools can create duplicate commit provenance records for the same hash when repo urls use different formats.
row.content: bug report from user: memory git provenance records may duplicate the same commit because repo identifiers are stored/searched in different formats, for example `github.com/j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app` versus `git@github.com:j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app.git`. this causes `memory_release_candidates_search` to return multiple candidates for the same commit hash, and `memory_release_notes_preview` can show both normal release bullets and a needs-context entry for the same commit. recommended fix: normalize repo urls before storing and searching so `git@github.com:j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app.git`, `https://github.com/j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app.git`, and `github.com/j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app` converge to `github.com/j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app`; dedupe by `normalized_repo + commit_hash`; apply the same dedupe in release notes preview.

row.title: repo url normalization bug confirmed in git memory code
row.summary: read-only investigation confirmed git memory commit records only lowercase/trim repo strings, so different url formats are not canonicalized or deduped.
row.content: investigation result: the duplicate commit candidate bug is code-related. in `extensions/memory/src/commit-changelog.ts`, repo handling uses `normalizetext`, which only trims and lowercases strings. `buildcommitmetadata`, `buildcommitpayload`, `addcommitrecord`, `findactiveduplicatecommit`, and `passesstructuredfilters` compare/store raw normalized text, so `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`, and `github.com/owner/repo` remain distinct. `searchreleasecandidates` returns all matching active commit records without deduping by repo/hash, and `previewreleasenotes` iterates those candidates directly, so duplicate records can appear as both release bullets and needs-context. existing tests only cover exact same repo-string dedupe and current head storage preserving the full https remote url; they do not cover cross-format repo canonicalization for commit records. `parsegitremote` in `context.ts` already canonicalizes project ids for git remotes but is not used by commit/changelog provenance code.

row.title: fixed git memory repo url dedupe bug
row.summary: implemented canonical repo url normalization and dedupe for git memory commit records, release candidates, and release notes preview.

row.title: sdd implementation map artifact policy
row.summary: formal sdd now uses a separate implementation-map.md artifact for operational handoff instead of storing file/symbol/validation details in metadata.yaml.
row.content: decision/progress: the sdd workflow was updated to introduce `openspec/changes/<change>/implementation-map.md` as a separate operational handoff artifact for formal openspec/hybrid sdd flows. the map is for explored files, relevant symbols, expected files to modify/create/delete, behavioral findings, constraints/risks, validation commands, open questions, and downstream handoff notes. it is explicitly separate from `metadata.yaml` and non-normative relative to metadata, approved prd, spec, design, and tasks. updated `skills/sdd-workflow/skill.md` plus sdd phase subagents (`sdd-explore`, `sdd-proposal`, `sdd-spec`, `sdd-design`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-apply`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-archive`) so phases read/update/preserve the implementation map according to their responsibilities. validation: `skill_registry_generate` reported 11 skills and unchanged generated artifacts; `skill_registry_resolve` routed sdd implementation-map paths to `sdd-workflow`; `git diff --check` passed. prd workflow was intentionally left for a separate future discussion.

row.title: prd workflow review findings
row.summary: read-only review found prd flow is conceptually sound but lacks a canonical prd template and explicit approval/readiness handoff semantics.
row.content: read-only review of prd flow: `sdd-workflow` currently makes prd optional, orchestrator-authored, and reviewed by `prd-review` when readiness is uncertain. `prd-review` checks ambiguity, contradictions, testability gaps, metadata alignment, security/privacy risks, and readiness for downstream sdd. strengths: prd drafting stays with orchestrator/user context; review is separate; critical debts block implementation; downstream sdd phases treat approved prd as context and must flag conflicts. gaps: no canonical prd template in `sdd-workflow`; no explicit prd status marker/approval handoff beyond conversation/orchestrator decision; prd review does not produce a structured requirement/acceptance-criteria coverage matrix for downstream spec; downstream phases read prd only when supplied/requested, which can allow prd context to be dropped; prd vs proposal responsibilities overlap and may duplicate product-level content; no explicit rule that prd must avoid implementation/file-level details now covered by `implementation-map.md`. potential future change: add a prd template and lifecycle states, require approved prd context handoff when a prd exists and is in-scope, clarify prd/proposal boundary, and ensure prd review outputs structured acceptance criteria/questions for sdd.

row.title: workflow triage aligned with prd lifecycle
row.summary: updated workflow-triage so prd-first routing knows about canonical prd structure, prd lifecycle/readiness, mandatory approved prd handoff, and implementation-map boundaries.
row.content: progress: after user noted that `workflow-triage` also helps choose prd/sdd routing, `skills/workflow-triage/skill.md` was aligned with the prd workflow changes. it now says prd review validates acceptance-criteria coverage and implementation-detail leakage, approved/in-scope prds must be read and preserved downstream, waived review requires stated risks, prds should use the canonical structure from `sdd-workflow`, and existing prd flows must carry approved prd context alongside metadata, phase artifacts, and `implementation-map.md`. validation: `skill_registry_generate` reported 11 skills and unchanged generated artifacts; `skill_registry_resolve` for prd-first sdd matched `sdd-workflow` and `workflow-triage`; `git diff --check` passed.

row.title: agents guide delegates detailed workflow rules to skills
row.summary: agents.md was simplified to keep high-level workflow policy while delegating detailed prd/sdd artifacts and routing semantics to workflow-triage and sdd-workflow.
row.content: decision/progress: `agents.md` was updated to reduce duplicated sdd/prd details and avoid drift. it now states that `workflow-triage` owns route selection and `sdd-workflow` owns detailed prd/sdd/openspec operations, including prd lifecycle, existing-prd handling, artifact policy, implementation-map rules, phase sequencing, subagent checklists, and return envelopes. the explicit stale openspec artifact list was removed from agents; metadata is described only as change control context, while detailed prd lifecycle, implementation-map handoff, artifact names, and phase formats live in `sdd-workflow`. prd guidance in agents now stays high-level and defers approved/in-scope prd handling and implementation-detail boundaries to `sdd-workflow`. validation: `git diff --check` passed and grep found no old contradictory agents wording such as canonical artifact list or downstream prd continuing only from metadata.

row.title: workflow gate wording tightened
row.summary: updated agents.md workflow selection wording to require workflow selection for all code edits/implementations and non-trivial docs/config changes.

row.title: websearch tools return insufficient full-text details
row.summary: bounded smoke tests showed several websearch tools do not provide enough complete text for reliable agent analysis.
row.content:
idea type: bug/usability finding
context: during a live smoke test of the pi websearch tools on 2026-06-19, search tools and detail tools were evaluated for whether they provide enough complete text for the agent to read and reason from.
concrete details: search_stack_overflow/search_github_issues/search_devto_articles/search_hackernews returned mostly title + url only. stack_overflow_question_get returned only title + url for the question, without the question body. stack_overflow_answers_get returned answer html but truncated with an ellipsis. github_issue_get returned issue body but appeared cut mid-word. search_devto_articles did not expose article_id, so devto_comments_get cannot be used directly from search output. search_hackernews did not expose story_id, so hackernews_story_get cannot be used directly from search output.
implications: future agents should treat current websearch output as useful for discovery but not sufficient for complete-text analysis. a follow-up fix should add ids, snippets, bodies/comments with explicit truncation metadata, and avoid silent mid-word truncation while preserving bounded output and read-only constraints.
source: live tool smoke test in current session.

row.title: github cli comments offset only works for aligned pages

idea type: bug
context: live smoke testing after implementing the `gh` github provider for websearch.
concrete details: `github_issue_get` on `nodejs/node#58380` with `commentslimit=4` and `commentsoffset=2` displayed numbering starting at 3 but returned the first page's comment bodies (`aduh95`, `mcollina`, `davidfiala`, `filipoliko`) instead of true comments 3-6. aligned offsets such as `commentsoffset=4` with `commentslimit=4` returned expected comments 5-8. cause is likely the client converting offset to `page = floor(offset / limit) + 1` and relying on github page pagination without slicing for non-aligned offsets. future fix should fetch enough comments from the containing page and slice locally, or use a stable per_page/page strategy that honors arbitrary offset semantics.

row.title: youtube transcript repair research findings
row.summary: community evidence and code inspection indicate youtube transcript failures should be handled by staged fallback and clear diagnostics rather than assuming captions are permanently disabled.
row.content:
type: learning
context: youtube-research extension repair investigation
findings: the extension uses yt-dlp for youtube transcript sources and fetches. community reports in yt-dlp/yt-dlp#13831 and youtube-transcript-api#303 show that youtube often returns transcript/subtitle failures because of ip/cloud blocking, anti-bot fingerprinting, translated/automatic subtitle rate limits, or 429s, even when captions exist in browser. yt-dlp maintainers recommend considering current/nightly yt-dlp, curl_cffi/impersonation where applicable, and handling subtitle fetch failures gracefully; comments also note json3 retries may sometimes work better than vtt.
code implication: extensions/youtube-research currently builds a transcript plan, but runtranscriptget selects one candidate and if client.fetchtranscript fails or returns empty, it fails without trying remaining best-effort candidates or metadata fallback. restrictive modes can remain strict, but auto/best-effort should likely iterate candidates, collect failed attempts, and fallback to description/chapters/metadata with clear diagnostics.
source: current session research on 2026-06-19 using github issue/release tools and code inspection.

row.title: websearch search operators are provider hints
row.summary: web_search passes operator-style queries through unchanged; site: works in practice, but negative and exact operators are not guaranteed.
row.content: note: live/code verification of web_search operator behavior. implementation passes query strings unchanged to providers: exa sends `query: input.query`; parallel sends `objective: input.query` and `search_queries: [input.query]`. the extension itself does not parse, normalize, enforce, or strip search operators. live tests showed `site:developer.mozilla.org "url() constructor"` returned developer.mozilla.org results and `site:nodejs.org url constructor base input typeerror` returned nodejs.org results, so `site:` works as a practical provider hint/filter with exa. however, `"url() constructor" -mdn web apis javascript` still returned mdn results, so negative operators and exact-match semantics are not strict guarantees. implication for agents: use operators as ranking/filtering hints, verify result domains/urls in returned metadata, and use web_fetch on selected urls for correctness-sensitive work.

row.title: exa and parallel search parameter support
row.summary: exa and parallel support different search parameter sets; mcp endpoints are more limited than direct apis.
row.content: note: investigated provider search parameters for the websearch extension. current code exposes only `query` and `limit`. exa provider calls hosted exa mcp `web_search_exa` with `query`, `type: fast`, `numresults`, `livecrawl: fallback`, and `contextmaxcharacters`; reliable basic params are `query` and `numresults`, while hosted/docs/search results indicate `type`, `livecrawl`, and context limits are supported or tolerated. for domain/date/category filters, exa direct search api supports `type`, `numresults`, `category`, `userlocation`, `includedomains`, `excludedomains`, `startpublisheddate`, `endpublisheddate`, `moderation`, `additionalqueries`, and content/highlight/summary options; exa mcp also has optional `web_search_advanced_exa` for those advanced filters but must be enabled via the mcp tools parameter. parallel search mcp is intentionally simple: docs say to express date/domain constraints directly in `objective`/query rather than dedicated mcp parameters; current code passes `objective` and `search_queries`. parallel direct `/v1/search` api supports `objective`, `search_queries`, `mode`, `max_chars_total`, `session_id`, `client_model`, and `advanced_settings` including source_policy include/exclude domains and after_date, fetch_policy, excerpt_settings, location, and max_results. implication: adding provider-specific parameters to our public `web_search` requires either provider-specific api support or a normalized abstraction with graceful degradation; for mcp-only parallel, domain/date filters should remain query hints unless switching to direct api.

row.title: websearch normalized filter parameters implemented
row.summary: implemented optional normalized web_search filters with exa-native mapping, parallel query hints, and default limit 10.
row.content: progress: implemented normalized optional filter parameters for the websearch extension public `web_search` tool. behavior: `limit` now defaults to 10 and remains optional with max 10; accepted filters are `includedomains`, `excludedomains`, `afterdate`, `beforedate`, `location`, and `mode` (`fast`, `auto`, `deep`). exa provider maps advanced filters to `web_search_advanced_exa` native args (`includedomains`, `excludedomains`, `startpublisheddate`, `endpublisheddate`, `userlocation`, `type`) and uses basic `web_search_exa` when no advanced filters are present. parallel mcp maps filters into natural-language objective constraints plus operator-style query hints such as `site:domain`, `-site:domain`, `after:yyyy-mm-dd`, and `before:yyyy-mm-dd`. results now include `filters` and provider metadata may include `filter_application` with `native`, `query_hint`, and `unsupported`. files changed include web provider/schema/type/tool/summary modules, tests, and readme. validation: `cd extensions/websearch && npm test -- test/web-search.test.ts test/web-providers.test.ts test/registration.test.ts` passed; `cd extensions/websearch && npm run typecheck` passed; `cd extensions/websearch && npm test` passed with 22 test files and 93 tests.

row.title: exa advanced web search json response not parsed
row.summary: live reload validation showed web_search_advanced_exa returns json-in-text results that current parser treats as no results.
row.content: bug: after reload, live tests of `web_search` with normalized advanced filters showed exa advanced search falls back to parallel even for queries that should match, e.g. `next.js 16 cache components documentation` with `includedomains: ["nextjs.org"]`. direct read-only mcp inspection confirmed `web_search_advanced_exa` responds successfully with text/event-stream where `content[0].text` is a json string containing top-level keys `requestid`, `resolvedsearchtype`, `results`, `searchtime`, and `costdollars`; each result has keys such as `id`, `url`, `title`, and `text`. current provider parser only handles `title:`/`url:` text blocks via `parseexatext`, so it returns zero items and triggers parallel fallback. implication: fix should extend the exa parser to first attempt json parsing for advanced mcp payloads and map `results[].title`, `results[].url`, `results[].text`, optional `publisheddate`/`author`/`score`, while retaining the existing block parser for basic `web_search_exa`.

row.title: exa advanced json parser fix implemented

row.content: progress: fixed the websearch exa advanced mcp parser bug. context: live reload validation showed `web_search_advanced_exa` returned valid results as json inside `content[0].text`, but the provider only parsed `title:`/`url:` text blocks, so filtered exa searches appeared empty and fell back to parallel. change: `extensions/websearch/src/providers/web/exa.ts` now attempts json parsing first, maps `results[].title`, `url`, `text`/`snippet`/`highlights`, `publisheddate`, `author`, and `score`, and preserves json metadata such as `searchtime`, `costdollars`, and `requestid`; it still falls back to the existing block parser for basic exa output. test: updated `extensions/websearch/test/web-providers.test.ts` to assert exa advanced json-in-text parsing with normalized filters. validation: `cd extensions/websearch && npm test -- test/web-providers.test.ts` passed; `cd extensions/websearch && npm run typecheck` passed; `cd extensions/websearch && npm test` passed with 22 test files and 93 tests. note: live pi tool needs reload before validating the new parser through the registered tool.

row.title: web_fetch live validation across reddit docs raw json
row.summary: validated web_fetch behavior across reddit, old reddit, docs markdown, mdn/github html, raw text, json, truncation, and https-only rejection.
row.content: progress: live-tested web_fetch quality across multiple source types. reddit: `web_search` with `includedomains: ["reddit.com"]` successfully returned reddit thread content/snippets, but `web_fetch` on modern `www.reddit.com` returned only `reddit - please wait for verification`; `.json` returned http 403; `old.reddit.com` fetched successfully with correct title and large html, but excerpts are noisy with old reddit navigation. docs: `web_fetch` on next.js docs returned clean `text/markdown` with frontmatter and agent-friendly content; mdn and github issue html fetched with correct titles/links but excerpts start with navigation chrome. raw/plain/json: raw github readme returned clean `hello world!`; github api json returned valid json excerpt. safety/bounds: small `maxbytes` truncates and marks `truncated`; non-https `http://example.com` is rejected. implication: for reddit, prefer `web_search` snippets or rewrite to `old.reddit.com` for fetch when needed, but expect noise; for github issues use dedicated github tools for structured content; `web_fetch` is strongest for markdown/plain/json and ai-friendly docs pages.

row.title: j0k3r-pi project profile
row.summary: living project profile for j0k3r-pi
row.content:
project: j0k3r-pi
purpose: configure and extend the pi coding agent with local extensions, workflow guidance, subagents, code intelligence, and persistent memory.

stack:
- typescript and node.js.
- pi coding agent extension apis and tool integrations.
- sqlite-backed local memory.

architecture:
- independent pi extensions live under extensions/ and are validated from their owning package directories.
- agent operating policy lives in AGENTS.md; specialized workflow guidance lives in skills/; delegated roles live in subagents/.
- openspec stores durable sdd artifacts when the selected workflow requires them.

important directories:
- extensions/: pi extension implementations and package-level tests.
- skills/: reusable agent workflow and domain guidance.
- subagents/: delegated agent definitions.
- openspec/: active and archived sdd artifacts.
- .pi/: project-local extension configuration and generated state.

validated commands:
- cd extensions/memory && npm test
- cd extensions/memory && npm run typecheck

conventions:
- answer direct questions without turning them into unrequested work.
- clarification and investigation come before implementation when requirements or causes are unclear.
- use workflow-triage before non-trivial edits and strict tdd for non-trivial code changes.
- use code-research tools first for supported local source-code inspection.
- reload pi before runtime validation of extension tool or renderer changes.
- use lowercase-oriented english prose for memory retrieval consistency while preserving exact case for case-sensitive paths, commands, symbols, identifiers, versions, acronyms, and quoted literals.
- do not create commits, branches, tags, rebases, or pushes without an explicit user request.

active decisions:
- the canonical project profile is read and maintained explicitly through memory_project_profile.
- canonical project-profile content preserves original case so case-sensitive paths and identifiers remain accurate.
- session shutdown may summarize the session but must not mutate the canonical project profile.
- canonical project profiles do not consume regular startup memory slots.
- memory startup, search, list, and recall remain compact indexes with actionable IDs; full records are loaded explicitly.
- expanded full-record rendering wraps complete text without visual truncation while collapsed rendering remains compact.
- mutation, session, provenance, dry-run, import, export, and sync tools expose bounded agent-visible data needed for their documented next action.

current work:
- no active implementation is recorded; next work should come from the current conversation.

recent completed work:
- commit 6dd4f96 makes Memory tool results actionable, aligns injected guidance, excludes project profiles from regular startup slots, and preserves bounded privacy-safe output contracts.
- the mini-sdd fix-memory-tool-output-contracts passed independent verification, post-reload live smoke, archive, commit, and push to origin/main.
- commit 7380a7f made project profiles readable, explicit, case-preserving, and manually maintained.
- latest validation passed 119 Memory tests, typecheck, skill registry checks, and git diff checks.

risks:
- do not reactivate archived planning or research threads without explicit user confirmation.
- avoid turning the project profile into session history, raw command logs, or lists of touched files.
- expose full memory content only after explicit record/profile selection; keep compact indexes and safety reviews bounded.
- validate each extension from its owning package directory because the repository root has no package.json.

row.title: antigravity local provider session lifecycle and response parsing
row.summary: the antigravity-local pi provider now scopes one agy process per pi session, uses the first user prompt as agy startup prompt, and ignores empty planner responses while waiting for final transcript text.
row.content: idea type: architecture and runtime workflow. context: implementing the local antigravity/agy provider for pi in ~/.pi/agent/extensions/antigravity-local. details: the provider maintains one agy process per pi session id, kills that agy on session_shutdown, and reuses the same conversation and port for later prompts in the same pi session. the first prompt is sent as agy --prompt-interactive startup input instead of a dummy bootstrap prompt. later prompts use agentapi send-message. response parsing waits for non-empty model planner_response text and no longer treats empty planner_response entries as final output. implications: future agents should preserve session-scoped pid/conversation mapping and non-empty transcript parsing when modifying this provider. source: manual smoke tests and transcript inspection on 2026-06-24.

row.summary: subagent render mode is now driven by the global subagents.json base config and applies to inline subagent_run rendering, with optional project override still supported by the normal merged config loader.
row.content: updated subagents so render mode is resolved from the standard subagents configuration loader, which reads the global base config at ~/.pi/agent/subagents.json or pi_coding_agent_dir/subagents.json and merges project overrides from .pi/subagents.json. the inline subagent_run render path in tools.ts now uses this render mode for progress and final collapsed summaries, so claude mode affects the main execution flow instead of only the history panel. for manual testing in this repo, subagents.json was written at the project root because the current workspace is the global agent directory, and the temporary .pi/subagents.json override was removed to avoid masking the global value.

row.title: subagents renderers split by mode for inline flow
row.summary: separated subagent_run inline rendering into explicit opencode and claude render helpers so future fixes can target one mode without mixing logic.
row.content: implemented conditional renderer helpers in extensions/subagents/src/tools.ts for subagent_run inline flow: rendercallopencode/rendercallclaude, renderpartialopencode/renderpartialclaude, and renderresultopencode/renderresultclaude. render mode still comes from the global subagents config and now cleanly selects a dedicated rendering path. this keeps opencode and claude presentation logic isolated for future fidelity work while preserving current behavior behind the mode switch.

row.content: in extensions/subagents/src/tools.ts, task-mode subagent execution now listens for ctrl+b only when the active render mode is claude. pressing ctrl+b stops waiting in the foreground, returns a background-task result, and leaves the task running in background. opencode mode and explicit background mode keep their previous behavior. tests cover both the positive claude path and the negative opencode path.

row.content: confirmed project decision: do not further diverge or redesign the ctrl+, expanded execution/history panel renderer between claude and opencode right now. keep that surface aligned for both modes for the moment, and prioritize other changes first. future renderer work can revisit ctrl+, but current work should focus on other behavior or inline rendering changes instead of splitting the panel experience more.

row.title: find-symbol extension architecture
row.summary: created global pi extension find-symbol using native tree-sitter for ts/js symbol resolution
row.content: created a new global pi extension at ~/.pi/agent/extensions/code-research/ (previously named find-symbol) that registers a custom tool 'find_symbol'. it uses native tree-sitter bindings (tree-sitter 0.21.1, tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2, tree-sitter-javascript 0.23.1, tree-sitter-java 0.23.5, minimatch 10.2.5) to parse ts/js/java files and return structured symbol locations. architecture is modular: index.ts registers the tool, src/core/parser.ts caches parsers, src/core/resolver.ts orchestrates search with per-call parse cache and pluggable language adapters, src/languages/typescript.ts extracts symbols for ts/js, src/languages/java.ts extracts symbols for java. supports parameters path, symbol, language (ts/js/java/auto), kind, include_signature, include_code, scope, glob, and search_mode (exact/prefix/contains). include_code is restricted to function/method kinds and disabled for non-exact searches. finds private members including hash-private (#name) in ts and private fields/methods in java. handles abstract classes, type aliases, nested functions, constructors, getters, setters, static methods. interface implementation detection works syntactically via implements clause for ts and java. includes example fixtures in examples/typescript/, examples/javascript/, and examples/java/. tested with the spring project at ~/sias/app/back. tests run with vitest and pass.

row.title: function call tree only surfaces relevant callbacks on application invocations
row.summary: java function_call_tree now attaches callback nodes to application invocation nodes only when callback bodies contain meaningful nested calls, keeping output compact and readable.
row.content:
idea type: output heuristic decision
context: improving java function_call_tree readability for agent debugging, especially when application calls receive arguments containing stream/map/foreach lambdas.
concrete details: callback extraction now applies not only to external chain nodes but also to application invocation nodes. callback containers are attached to the invoked application node only when the callback body yields nested calls after filtering. this keeps callbacks anchored to the true parent call instead of leaving them hidden inside called_as, while avoiding noise for callbacks that only construct values or do not call meaningful methods.
implications for future agents: preserve the compact rule: show callback nodes only when they reveal real nested behavior that helps trace execution; do not explode every lambda or argument expression into separate nodes.
source: implemented and validated in code-research on 2026-06-25 with tests and real rootworkflowrestcontroller inspection.

row.title: typescript function-call-tree fails on real project file paths
row.summary: ts/js function_call_tree can index directories correctly but returns not_found for a real absolute file path because it indexes from cwd instead of the target file root
row.content:
type: bug
context: validating the code-research function_call_tree tool against /home/j0k3r/sias/app/front.
evidence: function_call_tree on /home/j0k3r/sias/app/front/app/routes/root/resenia.tsx with symbol loader, language ts, kind function returned not_found. find_symbol on the same file and symbol found loader at line 32. function_call_tree on the directory /home/j0k3r/sias/app/front/app/routes/root returned an ambiguous list that correctly included resenia.loader.
probable_cause: executetypescriptfunctioncalltree sets indexroot to cwd when the target path is a file instead of deriving a root from the target file or at least indexing the containing directory/project root. with pi cwd at /home/j0k3r/.pi/agent, the index never includes the target app file.
implication: ts/js tests currently cover relative file paths under a temporary project root, so this real-project absolute file-path regression was missed.

row.title: typescript tools derive project roots from nearest markers with source-root fallback
row.summary: ts/js code-research tools can reuse a shared project-root resolver that prefers nearest package or ts/js config markers and falls back to parent of app/src when markers are absent
row.content:
type: architecture
context: fixing ts/js function_call_tree for absolute file paths outside pi cwd.
decision: shared ts/js root resolution now lives in languages/typescript/shared.ts as resolvetypescriptprojectroot(targetpath, isdirectory). it searches upward from the target for the nearest project markers (package.json, tsconfig.json, jsconfig.json, bun/package/pnpm/yarn lockfiles, deno config). if none are found, it falls back to the parent of source roots like app or src, then finally to the target directory.
implication: future ts/js tools can index from a stable project root even when invoked on an absolute file path from outside the target repo. this specifically avoids accidental indexing from pi cwd and should be reused by the next ts/js tool that needs project-level indexing.

row.title: ts function-call-tree robust root resolution now indexes build artifacts and hits parser size limit
row.summary: after switching ts/js function_call_tree to project-root indexing, real projects with build outputs can fail with invalid argument because the index walks build files larger than the shared 1mb tree-sitter buffer
row.content:
type: bug
context: validating function_call_tree against /home/j0k3r/sias/app/front after adding robust ts/js project-root detection.
evidence: function_call_tree on real ts files now returns invalid argument instead of not_found. the derived project root is correct, but collectsupportedfiles in src/languages/typescript/function-call-tree.ts recursively indexes everything except node_modules and dot directories, so it includes build/server/index.js. that file is 1342276 bytes in sias front. parsing it directly with the extension's javascript parser and buffersize 1048576 reproduces the exact error: invalid argument.
probable_cause: parser.ts uses a fixed 1mb buffer. function_call_tree project indexing now scans generated build artifacts and other non-source files, so large bundled js trips the buffer before the target route file can be processed.
implication: fixing ts/js root resolution exposed a second issue. future remediation can either narrow indexed directories/files for ts/js source analysis, skip parse-failing files during directory indexing like find_symbol does, increase or dynamically size the parser buffer, or combine these approaches.

row.title: ts js function-call-tree should index application source not generated outputs
row.summary: for ts/js call trees the tool should be source-oriented and skip generated/framework output directories and parse-failing files instead of aborting the whole analysis
row.content:
type: decision
context: refining the purpose of function_call_tree after comparing the successful java output with failing ts/js behavior on a real react router project.
decision: ts/js function_call_tree indexes application code only. generated outputs and framework caches are excluded from recursive indexing (node_modules, build, dist, coverage, .next, .nuxt, .svelte-kit, .react-router, .turbo, .vite, .cache, out). if a remaining file still fails to parse, indexing skips that file rather than failing the whole call-tree request.
rationale: the tool is meant to give the agent a fast whole-function application call tree for debugging and understanding behavior, not to traverse compiled bundles or generated framework artifacts.

row.title: ts js function-call-tree now skips generated directories and parse failures

row.content:

change: added regression tests proving oversized bundled files under build no longer break call-tree execution for ts/js. updated ts/js function_call_tree indexing to exclude generated/framework output directories and to continue when a file parse throws. current exclusions are node_modules, build, dist, coverage, .next, .nuxt, .svelte-kit, .react-router, .turbo, .vite, .cache, and out.
validation: targeted ts/js tests passed, then full extension npm test and npm run typecheck passed with 50 tests green.
implication: real front-end projects with build artifacts should no longer fail with invalid argument before analyzing the requested application function.

row.title: ts js module resolution is now config-aware through shared import candidate resolution
row.summary: ts/js call-tree resolution now uses a shared config-aware import resolver that reads tsconfig or jsconfig baseurl and paths mappings for alias-aware module lookup
row.content:
type: architecture
context: extending ts/js function_call_tree so application recursion works across alias imports like ~/... in real projects.
decision: shared logic lives in languages/typescript/shared.ts. it loads tsconfig.json or jsconfig.json from the derived project root, parses compileroptions.baseurl and compileroptions.paths, builds candidate module file paths for both relative and alias imports, and exposes alias matching for source classification. function_call_tree ts/js now resolves imported callables/classes through this shared config-aware resolver.
implication: future ts/js tools can reuse the same project-config-driven import resolution instead of treating all non-relative imports as libraries.

change: added failing tests for ts and js fixtures using tsconfig paths alias mapping, then implemented shared project-config-aware import candidate resolution and alias classification. targeted alias tests passed and the full extension suite is green.

row.title: ts js find-symbol now indexes destructured exported bindings
row.summary: extended shared ts/js symbol extraction so destructured export bindings are discoverable, including function-valued bindings from local object literals and variable bindings forwarded from factory results
row.content:

row.title: memory import can fail when restoring sessions
row.summary: memory import merge may fail on backups with missing sessions because prompt rows are processed before session rows.
row.content:
idea type: bug
context: investigating the user report that pi memory import does not work in project j0k3r-pi.
observation: `.pi/memory-backups/memory-backup.jsonl` contains 180 memories, 410 memory_entities, 36 memory_sessions, and 680 memory_session_prompts. `memory_import` dry_run reported 0 inserted and 590 conflicts, but a safe id comparison showed 716 rows would be inserted by merge (36 sessions and 680 prompts).
reproduction: running the import loop against a temporary sqlite copy of the real memory db failed before modifying the real db with `foreign key constraint failed` on the first missing `memory_session_prompts` row, after 590 conflicts. the missing prompt referenced a session row that appears later in the jsonl file.
likely cause: `exportmemory` sorts backup records lexicographically by `type:id`, which places `memory_session_prompts` before `memory_sessions`; `importmemory` processes file order, so child prompt rows are inserted before parent session rows. dry_run also reports `inserted=0` instead of a would-insert count, making the behavior look like a no-op.
implication: future fix should import rows in dependency order (memories and memory_sessions before memory_entities, memory_links, and memory_session_prompts) and ideally expose a dry-run would-insert count in tool/command output.

row.title: fixed memory import session restore ordering
row.summary: memory import now restores missing sessions before prompts and reports dry-run would_insert counts.
row.content:
idea type: progress
context: follow-up to the bug where memory import failed when restoring backups containing missing sessions/prompts into a db that already had memory rows.
change: `extensions/memory/src/export-import.ts` now sorts import rows by dependency order before applying them: memories, memory_sessions, memory_entities, memory_links, then memory_session_prompts. this avoids foreign-key failures from inserting prompts before their parent sessions.
change: import results now include `would_insert`, and tool/command output includes the would-insert count so dry-run no longer looks like a no-op when rows are pending.
validation: added regression test `imports missing sessions before their prompts when existing memory rows conflict` in `extensions/memory/test/advanced.test.ts`; ran `cd extensions/memory && npm test`, `cd extensions/memory && npm run typecheck`, targeted regression test, and `git diff --check` successfully.
implication for future agents: after reloading pi, `/memory-import dry_run` or the `memory_import` tool should show pending insertions with `would_insert`; `merge` should handle session/prompt backups without the previous foreign-key failure.

row.title: subagents widget can crash pi on sqlite busy reads
row.summary: the claude background widget reads current-session subagent tasks via manager.listsessiontasks, but sqlite busy errors from history.listsessiontasks are uncaught and can terminate pi during render.
row.content: idea type: bug. context: after a pi crash with `error: database is locked`, investigation showed the subagents claude background widget calls `manager.listsessiontasks(cwd, sessionid).slice(0, 100)` from `index.ts`, which reaches `subagenthistorystore.listsessiontasks` in `src/history.ts`. the query is correctly scoped to `where cwd = ? and session_id = ?`, so it is not reading all history. the likely failure mode is sqlite contention on the global history db in delete journal mode with no busy timeout/retry and no read-side error boundary in the widget/panel path. writes in `subagentmanager.recordnow` are caught, but reads from `cachedpersistedsessiontasks` are not, so a transient `sqlite_busy` can bubble into tui render and crash pi. future fix should add busy timeout/retry or wal where appropriate, and make widget/panel reads degrade gracefully on locked db.

row.content: idea type: progress. context: user chose robust option for the subagents `database is locked` crash. changes made in `/home/j0k3r/pi-subagents-j0k3r`: `src/history.ts` now configures history sqlite connections with `pragma busy_timeout = 2000`, best-effort `pragma journal_mode = wal`, and best-effort `pragma synchronous = normal`; `src/manager.ts` now catches sqlite busy errors in `cachedpersistedsessiontasks` and returns cached current-session tasks or `[]` instead of letting render paths crash; `test/subagents.test.ts` adds a regression test for locked current-session history reads. validation: targeted vitest for current-session history passed, typecheck passed. full `npm run check` is blocked by two existing shortcut tests expecting `ctrl+w`, unrelated to sqlite changes.

(2) hard rules now always offer the route choice ('direct fix vs mini-sdd/proposal') unless truly trivial single-file; (3) new rule: multi-file or policy-sensitive changes must offer mini-sdd/proposal even when user ordered a direct fix; (4) routing-table simple-tdd row default changed to 'ask route first unless truly trivial'; (5) interpretation rule: 'do not upshift' does not mean 'default to simple-tdd silently'; (6) workflow-triage triggers.keywords broadened with fix verbs (fix, fix it, corrige, arregla, refactor, cambia, modify, update code, bug fix, patch, correct) — 37 unique keywords after de-dup; (7) skill_registry_resolve is now an edit-time preflight (not only sdd preflight) when routing is ambiguous or request involves fixing/refactoring; (8) sdd-workflow execution step 1 updated to assume workflow-triage already ran (mandatory gate) instead of 'if route unclear'; (9) workflow-triage description frontmatter updated to reflect mandatory scope so skill_registry_resolve prioritizes it for ordered fixes. review pass 2026-06-29 found and fixed 3 bugs from the first edit pass: duplicate execution step number 8, duplicate 'refactor' keyword, and sdd-workflow step 1 contradicting the mandatory gate. note: there is no harness-level auto_load/mandatory flag in the registry schema; row.title: confirmed sdd workflow policy updates
row.summary: mini-sdd now uses openspec by default, prd-review owns prd approval, simple-tdd requires lightweight verification, no-framework tdd must ask the user, artifact_store none is blocked without explicit no-persistence approval, and active sdd memory uses metadata_json.type.
row.content:
type: workflow decision
context: user reviewed the main agent workflow and explicitly confirmed corrections to apply to future agents.
decisions:
- mini-sdd and minimal delegated apply should store and work through openspec by default with lightweight artifacts, not artifact_store none.
- prd-review must approve a prd for downstream sdd; ready-with-warnings does not proceed unless the user explicitly says to continue with the prd as-is.
- simple-tdd still requires verification, but the verification is lighter than full sdd: focused validation plus changed-file/scope/risk self-review.
- when no test framework exists for code changes, agents must stop and ask the user which validation strategy to use; if the user does not know, present options with pros and cons and wait for a choice.
- formal sdd, mini-sdd, and minimal delegated apply must block on artifact_store none unless the user explicitly requested no persistence and enough context is embedded.
- active sdd flow memory should be identified with metadata_json.type = "sdd_feature_project_state" plus tags sdd, active-flow, and the change slug.
implication: future workflow edits and sdd orchestration should follow these rules unless superseded by a later explicit decision.

row.title: strict answer-first policy for user questions
row.summary: when the user asks a question, agents must answer directly and stop instead of inspecting, investigating, editing, or continuing work unless explicitly asked.
row.content:
type: workflow policy decision
context: the user explicitly clarified that the main agent was still working when messages were questions. the user wants strict answer-first behavior.
decision: questions are answer-only by default. when the user asks a question, the agent must answer directly and then stop. it must not inspect files, run tools, investigate, plan implementation, edit, or continue working unless the user explicitly asks for that work in the current message or a later message. if follow-up work is useful, the agent should offer it as an option and wait for the user's next instruction.
implication: future agents should treat questions as a hard stop after the answer, even if they believe investigation or implementation would help.

row.title: codegraph mcp design comparison for code-research
row.summary: investigated colbymchenry/codegraph and compared its mcp workflow/tool surface with pi code-research extension.
row.content:
learning type: external design comparison
context: user requested read-only investigation of https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph cloned to /tmp/pi-investigate-codegraph, focusing on operating model and mcp/tools rather than language support.
findings: codegraph is a global cli/mcp product with per-project .codegraph sqlite indexes, install/init workflow, auto-sync watcher, staleness banners, connect-time catch-up, and strong agent steering through mcp initialize instructions. it exposes one mcp tool by default, codegraph_explore, which returns relevant source, call paths, and blast-radius context; narrower tools (node/search/callers/callees/impact/files/status) exist but are hidden by default and re-enableable via codegraph_mcp_tools. pi code-research is a pi extension with five specialized tools (find_symbol, find_references, function_call_tree, reverse_function_call_tree, workspace_graph_status), explicit typed parameters, optional .pi workspace graph, and deterministic fallback to direct analyzers when graph data is disabled/unusable/insufficient.
implications: potential future direction for pi code-research is a hybrid approach: keep precise specialized tools, but consider adding an optional unified explore/context tool for discovery and architecture questions, plus stronger cross-tool guidance and possibly more actionable freshness/fallback signals. no implementation was approved in this investigation.
source: local clone and docs/code inspection on 2026-06-30.

row.title: websearch renderer stack overflow on large compact output
row.summary: websearch compact renderer can crash pi with rangeerror maximum call stack size exceeded when truncating very large tool result text.
row.content: bug observed from user-provided crash stack on 2026-07-02: pi exited due to uncaughtexception rangeerror: maximum call stack size exceeded. stack points to extensions/websearch/src/render/index.ts tokenize -> truncate -> clip -> compactdetaildata -> compactresult -> render. root cause analysis: tokenize uses tokens.push(...segmenttext(...)); when clip/truncate receives a very large websearch result/resulttext fallback, segmenttext returns a huge array and spread-pushing it can exceed the js call stack. future fix should avoid spread for segment arrays, preferably use an append loop or lazy token iterator, and add regression tests for truncating very large text/results.

row.summary: the screenshot tool now discovers mango ipc sockets when mango_instance_signature is missing
row.content: progress: extended the utils screenshot mango backend so list-windows can use the newer `mmsg get all-clients` api even when the pi process did not inherit `mango_instance_signature`. the implementation scans `xdg_runtime_dir` (or `/run/user/<uid>`) for the newest `mango-*.sock`, injects it into the command environment, and keeps the existing foreign-toplevel/legacy fallback. validation passed in `extensions/utils`: `npm test` (28 tests), `npm run typecheck`, and `git diff --check` for the touched utils files. live check still used `mango (bash)` because the running mango process was `/usr/bin/mango (deleted)`, so mango must be restarted before the new 0.14.4 ipc socket exists.

row.title: mango inactive window crop captures visible region
row.summary: mango mmsg can list inactive windows with geometry, but grim geometry capture captures the visible output region rather than the inactive window buffer
row.content: learning: after restarting mango 0.14.4, `screenshot(action=list-windows)` used `backend: mango (mmsg)` and listed multiple windows with ids and geometry. capturing discord by `windowid: 3` succeeded technically with `grim -g`, but the inline image showed the currently visible pi terminal because discord and pi reported the same geometry and `grim -g` crops the output region, not an inactive/occluded window buffer. implication: mango inactive window capture is not solved by geometry alone; accurate inactive capture requires focusing/raising the target window first or compositor support for toplevel image capture such as grim `-t`/foreign-toplevel image capture, which mango did not expose in prior checks.

row.title: mango lacks grim toplevel capture globals
row.summary: mango 0.14.4 does not expose the foreign-toplevel image capture protocols needed by grim -toplevel capture
row.content: learning: investigating inactive wayland window capture without focusing on mango 0.14.4 showed that the compositor exposes `zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1`, `ext_image_copy_capture_manager_v1`, `ext_output_image_capture_source_manager_v1`, and `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1`, but not `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` or `ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1`. `grim -t` failed for mango mmsg ids (`3`, `1`, `mango:3`, `discord`) with `compositor doesn't support the screen capture protocol`. the grim binary references `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` and `ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1`, and the wayland protocol says the latter creates capture sources from `ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1`. implication: true inactive toplevel capture in mango requires compositor support/patching for the ext foreign toplevel list + image capture source path, or another compositor-provided buffer capture api; `grim -g` cannot capture occluded windows.

row.title: hyprland supports grim toplevel capture
row.summary: hyprland exposes the foreign-toplevel image capture protocols needed for inactive window capture with grim -t
row.content: learning: in a hyprland session, `screenshot(action=list-windows)` used `backend: hyprland (hyprctl)` and listed discord and kitty windows. geometry capture with `grim -g` still captured the visible screen region, not an inactive/other-workspace window. hyprland exposed the required globals for true toplevel capture: `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1`, `ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1`, `ext_image_copy_capture_manager_v1`, and `zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1`. a temporary wayland helper using `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` listed identifiers such as `1800001a` for discord, `18000019` for pi kitty, and `1800001b` for nvim. running `grim -t 1800001a` produced a real discord png while the active window check showed kitty/nvim, demonstrating inactive toplevel capture without focusing is possible on hyprland if the screenshot tool resolves ext foreign toplevel identifiers and uses `grim -t`.

row.title: utils screenshot targeted windows hyprland only
row.summary: targeted screenshot window listing and capture now intentionally supports only hyprland
row.content: decision/progress: the utils `screenshot` tool was refactored so targeted window listing/capture is hyprland-only. mango and sway window backends were removed from the targeted-window implementation and documentation. full-screen screenshots still use the generic linux screenshot backends. hyprland window listing uses `hyprctl clients -j`; targeted window capture resolves `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` identifiers with a temporary wayland helper and uses `grim -t`, enabling inactive window capture without changing focus. validation passed in `extensions/utils`: `npm test` (25 tests), `npm run typecheck`, and `git diff --check` for touched utils files. future live use requires `/reload` before the pi tool registry sees the new implementation.

row.title: memory extension lazy session discovery findings
row.summary: read-only discovery found that memory sessions are created eagerly in lifecycle session_start and proposed a minimal lazy-on-first-user-message fix path.
row.content:
type: progress
context: user reported that the pi memory extension creates a memory session during startup/load, but desired behavior is lazy creation on the first real user message.
findings: discovery traced eager creation to extensions/memory/src/lifecycle.ts session_start hook calling ensurememorysession({ reopenclosed: true }), which can call startmemorysession in extensions/memory/src/sessions.ts and insert into memory_sessions before any prompt. before_agent_start in lifecycle.ts is the feasible lazy creation point, but it currently calls ensurememorysession unconditionally.
recommended next step: use simple tdd with review. add failing tests in extensions/memory/test/advanced.test.ts asserting session_start does not create a memory session, first non-empty before_agent_start creates/reuses/reopens it, startup memory-context injection still works, and the first prompt is captured. minimal implementation should remove eager ensurememorysession from session_start, guard empty prompts in before_agent_start, and likely use reopenclosed: true on the first real prompt to preserve resume behavior.
risks: completed-session reopen semantics, startup context injection timing, memory_start_chat remaining intentionally eager, tui/api modes depending on the same lifecycle events.
source: discovery subagent result in session session_j0k3r_j0k3r-pi_1783024057792_5141508ea627411f.

row.title: code-research find_references misses nested callable bodies
row.summary: find_references returns no refs for exported functions called inside nested functions/callbacks because the typescript fallback indexes only top-level declarations and skips nested callable boundaries.
row.content: resolved bug and follow-up improvement: `find_references` returned no refs for exported functions called inside nested functions/callbacks because the typescript fallback extracted calls only from top-level callable bodies and skipped nested callable boundaries. fixed in `extensions/code-research` by adding a focused failing test for nested typescript function bodies and allowing `find_references` to call `extractcalls(..., { includenestedcallablebodies: true })` while preserving default `function_call_tree` behavior. follow-up improvement: the `find_references` tool now enriches returned references with a trimmed `source_line` field read from `file:line`, and the human text output is compact (`path:line:column: source_line (kind in context)`) instead of raw json metadata. validated with `vitest run test/find-references.test.ts --testnamepattern "nested function bodies"`, `vitest run test/extension-entry.test.ts --testnamepattern "find_references through"`, focused suites `test/find-references.test.ts test/extension-entry.test.ts test/reverse-function-call-tree.test.ts test/function-call-tree-typescript.test.ts test/function-call-tree-javascript.test.ts`, and `npm run typecheck`. note: the already-running pi tool process may need extension/session reload before the new compact output and `source_line` field are visible.

row.title: code-research graph reference metadata investigation
row.summary: workspace graph already persists typescript nested call edges with callsite text, but find_references bypasses graph due conservative coverage policy and graph callsites do not store full source_line.
row.content: implemented follow-up plus newly observed limitation: the persisted workspace graph shard for `extensions/memory` contains `calls` edges for `setcurrentmemorysessionid` from `registermemorylifecycle`, including `callsite.line`, `callsite.column`, and `callsite.text`. `find_references` now supports an explicit `reference_kinds` filter. when the caller requests graph-covered kinds such as `['call']`, graph policy marks coverage as supported and `find_references` can return graph-backed direct call references without rebuilding/parsing the full project. the graph query also matches directory-scoped targets such as `path: 'extensions/memory/src'`. the tool layer enriches `source_line` live from `file:line`, avoiding persistence of full source lines in graph shards and reducing privacy/secrets risk. default `find_references` with no `reference_kinds` remains complete/conservative and falls back to live scanning for callbacks, reads/writes, type refs, and imports. new limitation discovered by probing `getcurrentmemorysessionid`: graph fast-path with `reference_kinds: ['call']` returned no refs, while full fallback found two refs in `extensions/memory/src/tools.ts` where calls appear inside call arguments/object-literal values. likely cause: `workspace-graph.ts` `extracttypescriptcalls` returns after recording an outer call expression and does not descend into call arguments, so nested call expressions such as `searchmemory(... getcurrentmemorysessionid() ...)` are not persisted as edges. future fix should make graph typescript call extraction descend into call-expression children after recording the outer call, similar to `extractcalls(..., { includenestedcallablebodies: true })`, with tests ensuring nested argument calls are graph-backed. validated current implementation with graph-backed tests, fallback filter tests, focused suites, typecheck, and real probes.

row.title: workspace services extension manual configuration design
row.summary: confirmed design for a pi extension that manages monorepo services via explicit workspace configuration, per-service logs, state, and env-file opt-in.
row.content: decision: build a pi workspace services extension with manual configuration only. context: user wants an agent toolset to manage services in monorepos such as ~/sias/app without guessing services. details: use a workspace config like .pi/workspace-services.json with services keyed by service name; those keys are also the log base names. each service declares type (node or spring), path, command, and env_file boolean. env files are loaded only when env_file is true. runtime logs and state live under .pi/workspace-services/, e.g. logs/<service>.log and state.json. the extension should ensure .pi/workspace-services/ is ignored in .gitignore because it is local runtime state. expose separate tools: workspace_services_list, workspace_service_start, workspace_service_logs, workspace_services_status, workspace_service_restart, and preferably workspace_service_stop. source: user confirmed the proposed design on 2026-07-03.

row.title: browser full-page screenshot investigation
row.summary: terminal-only browser screenshot tools either require cdp or launch a separate browser; existing-tab full-page capture needs a browser companion extension when cdp is not active.
row.content: learning: terminal tests and web research confirmed that hyprland/grim can detect and capture the visible chrome window, but cannot list browser tabs or capture content beyond the viewport. current chrome process did not expose cdp: no remote-debugging flags, no devtoolsactiveport file, and local probes on common cdp ports returned no response. existing cli tools such as capture-website-cli, pageres-cli, shot-scraper, chrome headless screenshot, firefox screenshot, and playwright/puppeteer launch or connect to a browser and are useful for url screenshots but not for an already-open non-cdp tab. cdp-based clis such as agent-chrome-cli/chrome-remote-interface require a remote debugging endpoint. for an existing chrome tab without cdp, the practical architecture is a custom chrome companion extension using tabs + chrome.debugger page.capturescreenshot and a pi extension broker/tool layer, optionally using websocket or native messaging. hyprland remains useful for window correlation and visible-window fallback only. source: terminal probes and web/github research on 2026-07-03.

row.content: learning: after launching chrome with --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 --remote-debugging-port=9222 and a separate --user-data-dir, cdp capture worked. test details: fetched /json/list, selected page target sias at http://localhost:5173/, connected to its websocketdebuggerurl using node 24 built-in websocket, called page.enable, page.getlayoutmetrics, and page.capturescreenshot with format png, fromsurface true, capturebeyondviewport true, and clip from content size. output: /tmp/pi-cdp-fullpage-test.png, 56627 bytes, 1912x985. implication: a native pi browser screenshot tool can implement cdp direct capture for debug-profile chrome tabs without mcp. note: this specific page was not taller than viewport, so long-page tiling/lazy-load handling remains to validate separately.

row.title: reload pi before validating extension runtime changes
row.summary: pi must be reloaded before runtime tools and renderers reflect extension source changes.
row.content:
type: workflow constraint
context: pi extensions are registered when the pi process or session loads.
details: after changing extension source code, reload pi before testing the live tool output or renderer. tests that instantiate the extension directly can validate code before reload, but the currently registered runtime may still use the previous implementation.
implication: do not interpret pre-reload live tool behavior as evidence that the new extension code failed.
source: explicit user instruction on 2026-07-20.

row.title: memory tool and injected prompt contract audit
row.summary: audit of all 26 memory tools found critical agent-visible output gaps and prompt contradictions; implementation should proceed through a mini-sdd.
row.content:
type: discovery finding
context: all 26 registered memory tools were exercised on 2026-07-20 using live read-only calls plus an isolated temporary sqlite database and git repository for mutating operations.
details:
- critical retrieval gaps: memory_get hides full content and memory_recall hides candidate ids and snippets from agent-visible text.
- action continuity gaps: memory_add, update, archive, session creation/finish, and commit/changelog/release creation hide canonical ids needed by later actions.
- safety review gaps: memory_consolidate dry-run hides candidate groups; memory_import dry-run hides conflict and project-profile collision details; memory_sync_status hides counts.
- rendering gap: general expanded memory rows clip content at 600 characters; project-profile rendering is the working reference contract.
- schema mismatch: memory_record_current_commit marks rich provenance fields optional although runtime requires summary, functional_description, changelog_bullets, change_type, and release_impact.
- prompt conflicts: forced lowercase rules conflict with case-sensitive literals; profile updates are ambiguously assigned to memory_add and memory_project_profile; memory_start_chat guidance conflicts with automatic lifecycle startup; memory_get guidance excludes valid ids from list, recall, and startup; project_profile still consumes a startup slot despite the decision not to inject it.
- intentional compact contracts that worked: memory_search, memory_list, release candidate search, commit/changelog search, and release notes preview.
implications: prepare a mini-sdd that prioritizes complete memory_get, actionable compact recall, visible ids for mutation workflows, inspectable dry-runs, full expanded rendering, schema alignment, and prompt cleanup while preserving intentionally compact indexes.
source: orchestrator runtime audit plus independent discovery review; no production memory or code was modified during the audit.

row.title: git memory search renderer label may be incorrect

row.content:
type: discovery finding
context: a read-only git memory audit was attempted in another project with git.enabled=true but no synchronized commit/changelog records.

- memory_commit_changelog_search returned zero results and rendered as memory_search.

row.title: memory lifecycle sessions use the pi session id

row.content:
type: architectural decision
context: the user confirmed the desired memory lifecycle identity while defining reliable manual and automatic session closure.
decision: for lifecycle-managed sessions, memory_sessions.id must equal the exact pi session id returned by the pi session manager. memory_session_finish may omit session_id and resolve the current pi session id automatically.

row.title: memory backup import/export is not exact multi-machine synchronization
row.summary: current jsonl backup flow copies rows but cannot propagate deletions or safely reconcile concurrent updates between machines.
row.content:
idea type: discovery finding
context: read-only analysis of `extensions/memory/` import/export behavior for git-mediated synchronization between machines.
observed behavior: mirror export removes locally absent rows from the backup, but import never deletes local rows absent from the snapshot. merge export preserves absent rows and therefore cannot propagate deletion. import treats every existing id as a conflict without comparing row hashes; keep_local ignores remote updates, keep_imported overwrites blindly, and mark_conflict does not establish a causal merge. manifest hashes and brain_id are written but not used for reconciliation or integrity validation. there is no persisted imported/exported generation, mutation/tombstone journal, stale-backup preflight, or lifecycle warning that an import is pending.
implication: exact multi-machine sync requires a versioned generation protocol, explicit tombstones or authoritative reconciliation, local sync state/outbox, hash-checked transactional import, and export blocking when the on-disk generation has not first been imported or reconciled.
source: observed in `extensions/memory/src/export-import.ts`, `sync-status.ts`, `memory-store.ts`, `migrations.ts`, `tools.ts`, and `lifecycle.ts` during the current investigation.

Necesitamos adaptar esta extensión para integrarse con pi-subagents-j0k3r usando el canal genérico de interacción.         
                                                                                                                              
   Problema actual:                                                                                                           
   - Cuando un tool dentro de un subagent necesita interacción humana, la extensión devuelve algo como:                       
     `non_interactive_ask_denied: Approval could not be collected...`                                                         
   - Eso falla cerrado dentro del subagent y nunca sube la solicitud al orquestador principal.                                
                                                                                                                              
   Nuevo comportamiento requerido:                                                                                            
   - Si la extensión detecta que está corriendo dentro de una sesión subagent, no debe negar inmediatamente por modo no       
 interactivo.                                                                                                                 
   - Debe emitir una solicitud estructurada genérica `interaction_required`.                                                  
   - pi-subagents-j0k3r registrará sesiones subagent en:                                                                      
     `Symbol.for("pi.subagents.interactionSessions")`                                                                         
   - Las solicitudes pueden publicarse en:                                                                                    
     `Symbol.for("pi.subagents.interactionChannel")`                                                                          
   - Las respuestas del padre se consumirán desde:                                                                            
     `Symbol.for("pi.subagents.interactionResponses")`                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
   Contrato de request:                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                              
   {                                                                                                                          
     "type": "interaction_required",                                                                                          
     "requestId": "stable-unique-id",                                                                                         
     "kind": "approval-or-specific-kind",                                                                                     
     "origin": "subagent",                                                                                                    
     "requester": {                                                                                                           
       "subagentName": "...",                                                                                                 
       "taskId": "..."                                                                                                        
     },                                                                                                                       
     "prompt": {                                                                                                              
       "title": "...",                                                                                                        
       "message": "...",                                                                                                      
       "choices": ["Allow once", "Deny"]                                                                                      
     },                                                                                                                       
     "payload": {                                                                                                             
       "include all structured data needed to answer and later apply the decision"                                            
     },                                                                                                                       
     "response": {                                                                                                            
       "expected": "choice"                                                                                                   
     }                                                                                                                        
   }                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                              
   También puede devolverlo en el tool result details:                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
   {                                                                                                                          
     "details": {                                                                                                             
       "interactionRequest": {                                                                                                
         "payload": { ...interaction_required... }                                                                            
       }                                                                                                                      
     }                                                                                                                        
   }                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                              
   o publicarlo en el registry global:                                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
   const key = Symbol.for("pi.subagents.interactionChannel");                                                                 
   const registry = globalThis[key] ?? new Map();                                                                             
   globalThis[key] = registry;                                                                                                
   registry.set(handle, {                                                                                                     
     handle,                                                                                                                  
     payload: interactionRequest,                                                                                             
     createdAt: new Date().toISOString()                                                                                      
   });                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
   Luego el subagent será reintentado. En el reintento, la extensión debe buscar la respuesta en:                             
                                                                                                                              
   const responseKey = Symbol.for("pi.subagents.interactionResponses");                                                       
                                                                                                                              
   por `requestId`, y aplicar la decisión recibida.                                                                           
                                                                                                                              
   Importante:                                                                                                                
   - No crear un canal específico para permisos.                                                                              
   - No usar nombres `permission_required` ni `permission_channel`.                                                           
   - Todo debe ir por `interaction_required` / `interaction_response`.                                                        
   - El request debe incluir suficiente `prompt`, `payload` y `response` para que el padre pueda resolver cualquier           
 interacción humana.                                                                                                          
   - Por defecto debe seguir fallando cerrado si no está dentro de una sesión subagent o no hay respuesta disponible.         
   - Agregar tests: emisión de `interaction_required`, consumo de `interaction_response`, fallback seguro cuando no hay
